subject: physiology
title: The Enteric Nervous System, Slow Waves, and Interstitial Cells

steps.tx: Possessing over five hundred million neurons distributed along the gastrointestinal tract, the **enteric nervous system** functions as a quasi-autonomous third division of the autonomic nervous system. It coordinates local peristalsis, mucosal blood flow, and fluid secretion independently of extrinsic input from the brain or spinal cord.
steps.say: The enteric nervous system contains over five hundred million neurons, regulating gut motility and secretion semi-autonomously.

left.title: Myenteric (Auerbach) Plexus
points: Located between outer longitudinal and inner circular muscle layers
Extends continuously from upper oesophagus to internal anal sphincter
Governs gastrointestinal motility, tone, and contraction velocity
Inhibited by sympathetic outflow; stimulated by parasympathetic input

right.title: Submucosal (Meissner) Plexus
points: Located in submucosal space between circular muscle and mucosa
Most prominent in small and large intestine; sparse in oesophagus
Controls local mucosal secretion, absorption, and submucosal blood flow
Integrates sensory afferents from mucosal luminal chemoreceptors

steps.tx: Situated between the outer longitudinal and inner circular smooth muscle layers, the **myenteric plexus**, or Auerbach plexus, regulates gut motility. Activation of myenteric neurons increases tonic contraction of the gut wall, accelerates the velocity of peristaltic wave conduction, and coordinates receptive relaxation of downstream sphincters.
steps.say: The myenteric plexus lies between muscle layers, controlling contraction rhythm, tone, and sphincter relaxation.

vis.caption: Enteric ganglionated nerve plexuses, neuromuscular junctions, and congenital aganglionosis in gut motility.

steps.tx: Situated within the submucosa, the **submucosal plexus**, or Meissner plexus, senses luminal chemical and mechanical conditions. It regulates localized secretion of digestive enzymes, bicarbonate, and water, while modulating mucosal blood flow through the release of vasoactive intestinal peptide and acetylcholine.
steps.say: The submucosal plexus monitors luminal chemistry to regulate mucosal secretion and localized microvascular blood flow.

steps.tx: Rhythmic, spontaneous oscillations in smooth muscle resting membrane potential that dictate gut contraction frequencies are designated **electrical slow waves**. Slow waves do not represent true action potentials themselves, but rather subthreshold depolarizations that bring smooth muscle cells closer to mechanical threshold.
steps.say: Slow waves are rhythmic subthreshold depolarizations that establish the baseline electrical rhythm of the digestive tract.

rows: Rapid mixing with bile and pancreatic juice

steps.tx: The specialized physiological pacemakers of the gastrointestinal tract that generate slow waves are the **interstitial cells of Cajal**. Forming an interconnected syncytial network with surrounding smooth muscle cells via gap junctions, these mesenchymal pacemaker cells express transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase KIT.
steps.say: Interstitial cells of Cajal serve as gut pacemakers, generating slow waves through periodic ion fluxes.

nodes.label: Interstitial Cells of Cajal (ICC) Undergo Spontaneous Intracellular Ca2+ Oscillations
Activation of Anoctamin-1 (ANO1) Calcium-Activated Chloride Channels
Slow Wave Depolarization Spreads via Gap Junctions to Smooth Muscle Syncytium
Voltage-Gated L-Type Ca2+ Channels Open -> Spike Action Potentials and Contraction

steps.tx: When slow wave depolarizations exceed minus forty millivolts, voltage-gated L-type calcium channels open, generating **spike potentials and contraction**. Greater amplitude and duration of slow waves increase the frequency of superimposed calcium spike potentials, producing stronger, phasic smooth muscle mechanical contractions.
steps.say: Spike potentials occur when slow waves cross the threshold, letting calcium rush in to trigger smooth muscle contraction.

left.title: Electrical Slow Waves
points: Generated by interstitial cells of Cajal pacemakers
Occur constantly whether contractions take place or not
Dictate maximum possible frequency of contraction

right.title: Spike Action Potentials
points: True action potentials elicited when slow wave exceeds -40 mV
Mediated by influx of extracellular Ca2+ through L-type channels
Directly triggers calmodulin-myosin light chain phosphorylation
Enhanced by acetylcholine and gastrin; inhibited by adrenaline

steps.tx: Congenital failure of neural crest cells to migrate into the distal bowel during embryonic development produces congenital megacolon, known as **Hirschsprung disease**. The absence of myenteric and submucosal plexuses in the aganglionic distal rectum prevents receptive relaxation, causing severe functional obstruction and proximal colonic dilation.
steps.say: Hirschsprung disease is congenital absence of enteric ganglia in the distal colon, causing severe constipation and megacolon.

vis.alt: Enteric ganglion loss and neuromuscular aperistalsis
vis.caption: Pathophysiological failure of enteric inhibitory neurons, tonic muscular spasm, and lumen obstruction.

steps.tx: Neurotransmitters of the enteric nervous system are functionally segregated into excitatory and inhibitory classes. While acetylcholine and substance P drive smooth muscle contraction, the primary **inhibitory enteric neurotransmitters** are nitric oxide and vasoactive intestinal peptide, which mediate receptive relaxation ahead of advancing food boluses.
steps.say: Acetylcholine stimulates gut contraction, while nitric oxide and VIP mediate essential receptive relaxation ahead of food.
